## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `78fb73bfd49a4537e79199e94840cee9e6eec7b5`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #11810 (body and all five comments, 6043301317 triage / 6046638726 claim / 6048143784 dev report / 6048182477 claim amendment / 6048273522 dev addendum), PR #11836 (body, 17-file list, net diff against `main` at the head above, merge-base `8aebc6f`, 567 added / 19 removed lines), and the 43 check-runs on the head: 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` by design (`Test (coverage)`, its shard matrix, `dependabot`), 0 failure, 0 in progress; the one commit status (Vercel, ignored build step) `success`. Head repo is the base repo. No governed path in the file list (`.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` untouched), so this review is owed by the claim's amended `Clause-②: yes` (6048182477) alone. No earlier `## Contract review` record exists on the PR or the card. The spec facts in ①.10 are read from the shared objectstack checkout (`packages/spec` history and CHANGELOG) and from objectui's `scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs` and its workflow at `main`; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes (what the end-user list and the shared builder read and offer):

1. `ListView.filterFields` membership: a field whose served definition has `hidden === true` is dropped, unless `filterableFields` names it or a condition the panel holds filters on it. RIGHT: the spec declares `hidden: z.boolean().default(false)`, so the strict test is the right one; the two keep-rules satisfy the card's "hidden fields are not offered" without blanking a restored row's field trigger (pinned: a held `organization_id` keeps its label and goes last, `owning_business_unit_id` stays absent). The `filterableFields` whitelist is applied first, as before (#4243), so a hidden field the author named is an explicit choice.
2. Order: tier 0 the view's columns in `effectiveFields` order (after FLS, user-hidden columns and `fieldOrder`), tier 1 other business fields, tier 2 system fields through `isSystemManagedField(name, def)` (the spec `system` flag, then the name list), tier 3 a kept hidden field; the definition's order inside a tier. RIGHT against the triage direction ("fields follow the view's column order, system fields grouped last") and the signature in `@object-ui/types` `system-fields.ts`. A system field the author placed as a column sorts with the columns: the grid's own order, which is the card's "the view's columns, then the rest".
3. Default: `addCondition` is unchanged and seeds on `fields[0]`, so the first visible column leads and no second default is introduced. RIGHT (pinned: "Add filter" reads Title; ablation 1 reads Organization, the card's symptom).
4. Builder offer: `offeredOperatorsForRow` is `operatorsForFieldType` minus `is_null` / `is_not_null` on a `null_only` arm, with the row's own operator (normalised through the read boundary) always mounted. RIGHT: the arm is `@objectstack/spec`'s `expandEmptyOperator` (`multi_value` by `isMultiValueField`, `text` by `STRING_VALUE_TYPES`, else `null_only`), not a local list; every bucket that carries the nullness pair also carries `is_empty` / `is_not_empty` (text, number, date, select, lookup; boolean carries neither), so the pair that stays is offered wherever an empty check exists; the dialects lower `is_empty` to `$empty` (`FilterConditionField`, `datasetFilterCondition`, the grid AST's `isempty`), which the server expands to null-only on that arm, the same records as `$null`. The hold set `operatorsForFieldType` is unchanged (pinned), so `builderHolds` / `readBackOperator` and the plugin-list parity pin keep their answers, and a stored `is_null` on a select still loads (pinned, including the camelCase spelling).
5. The hint: rendered only when the row's offer holds both `is_empty` and `is_null` AND the arm is not `null_only` (so a held `is_null` on a select draws none), the two labels interpolated from the operator keys rather than restated. RIGHT: the ruling's "then a hint says how", verbatim.
6. The 7561 recorded number-column list loses the null pair; the de quote census moves 71 to 75 (two keys, two quoted spans each). RIGHT, both consequences of 4 and 8.
7. A `multiple: true` lookup / user / select is judged `null_only` because the builder's field descriptor (`FilterBuilderProps.fields`) carries `type` and no `multiple`, so it is offered the `is_empty` pair only. ACCEPTED as right: that pair is the one whose server expansion counts `[]`, which is the end user's reading; what is lost is only a fresh "Is null" on such a column (a stored one still loads). Adding `multiple` to the descriptor would be a new type member, correctly not done under this card. Noted for the seat; not a condition.

Public-surface changes (what a published package's accept set gains or claims):

8. `@object-ui/i18n`: two new keys, `filterBuilder.emptyCheckHint.text` and `.list`, in all ten packs. PUBLIC (`./locales` and `./locales/*` are in the package's `exports`) and RIGHT: additive only; every pack carries both the `isEmpty` and the `isNull` placeholder in both keys (`check:i18n-designer-parity` green); the nine non-en packs are translations, not copies (de in its own quote pair); the inline fallback in `filter-builder.tsx` matches the en text. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed.
9. `@object-ui/components`: no export, prop or type member added. RIGHT: `NULLNESS_PAIR`, `emptyCheckArm`, `offeredOperatorsForRow` and the hint renderer are module-private, and `operatorsForFieldType`'s contract is unchanged.
10. `@object-ui/components`' declared `@objectstack/spec` range. WRONG. The diff adds `import { expandEmptyOperator } from "@objectstack/spec/data"` to `filter-builder.tsx`, a module of the published entry, and the package's build keeps every bare specifier external (`vite.config.ts`: its `external` function answers true for every id that is not relative), so the published `dist/index.js` now imports that symbol from the spec. `expandEmptyOperator` first shipped in `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0`: it was added in objectstack `b810ddb6` while `packages/spec/package.json` read 17.4.0 (after 17.4.0 had been cut), and the spec CHANGELOG lists it under 17.5.0 and under no earlier version. `packages/components/package.json` still declares `"@objectstack/spec": "^17.0.0"` in `dependencies`, a range that admits 17.0.0 through 17.4.x, none of which export the symbol. A declared range is a public claim (objectui#5793, the ruling `scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs` is built on: floors track reality), and this repo's practice is to raise the importer's floor in the same PR and name it in the changeset (plugin-form `^17.0.0` to `^17.6.0` in #11623 for `deriveInlineGridColumns`; auth to `^17.3.0`; app-shell to `^17.6.0` in #11611). The base is honest today: `isFileIdToken`, components' only other runtime import from `@objectstack/spec/data`, is in 17.0.0, and the nightly `spec-range-floors` workflow is green on `main` (latest scheduled run, head `77c12b9`). This PR turns it red at the next nightly and at `changeset:publish`, whose script runs `check-spec-range-floors.mjs` before `changeset publish`, which blocks the whole fixed group's release. The head's check-runs cannot see it: that gate is deliberately not a `pull_request` job (its workflow header says so). The dev did not flag it, and the claim's File surface does not include `packages/components/package.json`.
    Remedy, one line and one sentence: in `packages/components/package.json`, `"@objectstack/spec": "^17.5.0"`; in `.changeset/11810-filter-builder-fields.md`, a sentence in the precedent's shape, "`@object-ui/components` raises its `@objectstack/spec` floor from `^17.0.0` to `^17.5.0`, because its published entry now imports `expandEmptyOperator`, which the spec first exports in 17.5.0." The seat adds the manifest to the claim's File surface. `@object-ui/plugin-list` and `@object-ui/i18n` need no move: their published sources import nothing new from the spec (the plugin-list test's `injectedSystemColumnDefs` is not published).
11. No REST path, query set, metadata schema or `@objectstack/*` import other than ①.10 changes; nothing in `packages/spec`-governed territory; nothing narrows. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/11810-filter-builder-fields.md` declares `@object-ui/i18n` `minor`, `@object-ui/components` `minor`, `@object-ui/plugin-list` `patch`; all three are in the `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`), so the group versions together at `minor`. `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Claim Re-read` and `Changeset Bump Policy` are all green on the head; no `major`.
- PR body line 2 carries `Clause-②: yes` at line start, copied from the amended claim; `yes` requires at least `minor`, and `minor` is declared. No `(widening)` / `(narrowing)` arm is written, which is correct: the arm is optional and nothing in the accept set narrows.
- The level matches what the diff publishes: the two i18n keys are the public addition that makes the clause `yes` (①.8); components' own code adds no surface (①.9) and its `minor` is the fixed-group reading precedent #11645 set; `patch` is right for plugin-list's ordering and filtering fix. The floor move ①.10 asks for does not change the level (precedent #11623 carried its floor move at `patch`; the group is at `minor` regardless), but it must be NAMED in the changeset body as the precedent names it, and the current body does not.
- The body names the behaviour, the two keys and the card, carries no model identifier, and needs no FROM-to-TO mapping because nothing is removed.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `open_questions[0]` (6048143784), land the hint and its keys under an amended `Clause-②: yes` (A) or drop commit `cedb17c` and carry the hint as a follow-up (B): the seat answered A (6048182477). I judge A right: the hint is the ruling's own text, B would ship text and list columns with two unexplained pairs, the confusion the card reports, and the two keys are copy in an existing namespace, additive, pinned on both arms. Closed.
2. `deviations`, files outside the claim's File surface (the ten packs and the de census pin): covered by the amendment's File-surface line. Closed. The same breach now recurs for `packages/components/package.json` (①.10) and needs the same amendment.
3. `deviations`, Zone 2 not booted live; the fixture rebuilt from the spec's `injectedSystemColumnDefs`, `task.object.ts` and the `__search` companion, pinned at 25 fields as a lit control (`organization_id` first, the three hidden names present): ACCEPTED. The fixture reproduces the card's observed shape, and the lit control makes a drift in either source loud.
4. `deviations`, `check:eager-closure` and `check:eager-locale-catalogues` NOT MEASURED locally: CLOSED BY CI. `Bundle Analysis` is `success` on the head and its comment on the PR (6048316806) reads PASS, eager closure 3521.7 KB against a 3551.8 KB budget (the dev's esbuild probe priced the new import at +94 B gzip).
5. `deviations`, the first ablation attempt a guarded no-op, re-run with a single-line anchor: a process note, not a boundary. The three ablations went red in the predicted direction with the restore proven.
6. Round-2 `deviations` (6048273522), `main` moved and the branch was not merged: not a condition. The PR reads `mergeable: true` / `clean`, and the gate verdicts are the head's own check-runs. `main` has moved again since; the push ①.10 asks for may rebase or not as the dev judges, since nothing in this diff touches what landed.
7. Round-2 `deviations`, the PR body's footer form: no model identifier in the title, body, changeset, code comments or the four commits' trailers (checked). Not a contract matter. Closed.
8. Acceptance notes: `multiple: true`, see ①.7, accepted; a system field that is a view column sorts with the columns, see ①.2, right; kept hidden fields go last, see ①.1, right; the Sort picker's hidden-field offer not measured, carrier none, together with the matching `out_of_scope_findings` entry: ESCALATED to the dispatching seat to decide whether ONE card is filed for it (the dev correctly did not POST issues; dedupe words as the report gives). Outside this card's step; not a condition.
9. A flag the report did not raise: the spec floor, ①.10. This is the FAIL condition. The dev's gates were the per-PR families; the family that judges floors runs nightly and at release, so no local or CI signal reached the dev. The miss is the convention's (raise the floor with the import), not a measurement failure, and it costs one commit.
10. The report's CI line (`in_progress` at report time): RESOLVED as in the inputs line above; nothing red, nothing pending.

What clears this record: one commit on the branch carrying the manifest line and the changeset sentence from ①.10, after which a fresh `## Contract review` is owed on the new head (this record names this head only).
